housing.summary: Oslo's rental market is competitive and among the most expensive in Norway; most listings are found via online portals and demand moves quickly, especially for central one-bedroom flats. Deposits are held in a dedicated tenant deposit account (depositumskonto).

banking.summary: Opening a Norwegian bank account requires a national identity number or D-number plus valid ID; account opening for newcomers typically follows registration with the tax authority. BankID is the standard digital identity used for banking and public services.
required_docs: D-number or Norwegian national identity number (fødselsnummer)
Employment contract or proof of address

schools.summary: Oslo offers Norwegian public schooling (free) as well as international schools serving expatriate families with English-language and international curricula. Public school placement is generally tied to the residential catchment area.

legal_admin.summary: EU/EEA nationals register with the police, while non-EEA nationals need a residence permit before arrival. Newcomers must report to the tax office for an ID check and register in the National Population Register to obtain a national identity number or D-number.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register with the National Population Register / report to the tax office (Skatteetaten) for ID check to obtain a D-number or national identity number; EU/EEA nationals also register with the police.

tax_finance.summary: Everyone working in Norway needs a tax deduction card (skattekort) and a national identity number or D-number. Income tax is administered by the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten), which issues the tax card based on expected income.
tax_finance.tax_id_name: D-number / national identity number (fødselsnummer); tax deduction card (skattekort)

transport.summary: Oslo has an integrated public transport network covering metro (T-bane), trams, buses and local ferries, operated under a single ticketing system with zone-based fares. Tickets and passes are bought via a mobile app or travel card.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA driving licences remain valid in Norway; licences from many non-EEA countries must be exchanged within a set period after residence, sometimes requiring a test.
transport.healthcare_registration: Residents register with a regular GP (fastlege) through the national health portal after obtaining a national identity number; access to the public health system follows registration.
